prompt: Create a production paper texture for a lovingly weathered old Vietnamese mountain-travel diary bound in indigo cloth. A perfectly flat orthographic scan, portrait 2:3. Fill the ENTIRE canvas with paper from edge to edge, no surrounding surface, no perspective, no book mockup. Visibly aged warm tan rag paper: muted antique buff and tea-stained parchment, approximately #d7bd91 across the broad center, never white or pale cream. Beautiful fine cellulose fibers, soft uneven grain and gentle desaturated umber mottling. This should look like paper that has traveled in a backpack for decades, tactile and poetic, not a Halloween scroll. The large central 84 percent is spacious, evenly illuminated and has low-contrast grain, keeping dark handwritten Vietnamese text clearly readable. All strong wear stays in the narrow outside margins: frayed fibers, tiny short edge tears with fine dark seams and pale exposed fibers, irregular foxing, worn corner creases, subtle old water tide marks. No dark stains crossing the center. No text, writing, letters, ruled lines, numbers, illustrations, symbols, photographs, objects, hands, folds across the center, or decorative border. No white vignette or white center, no glows. Not scorched, no burnt black edge. Watercolor-adjacent material realism, very high quality, quietly beautiful, natural dry matte paper, uniform flat lighting. This is a blank INNER BOOK COVER lining, slightly deeper and more muted brown tan approximately #c3a77e, dense handmade laid-paper fibers with an extremely faint linen impression, rubbed edges and old bookbinding glue shadows within the outermost 3 percent. Calm and blank throughout, no marbling pattern, no motifs, no broad dark areas. This material will appear briefly on the inside of the opening cover. Full-bleed rectangular paper texture.
